title: Why Do Bean Flower Clusters and Young Beans Rot?
content: Bean flower clusters and young beans may rot or drop due to climatic stress such as excessive heat, cold, sudden rain, or storms. Other causes include humidity imbalance, improper irrigation, nutrient deficiency, insect attack, disease, and the sensitivity of certain varieties.

title: How to Prevent Bean Flower Clusters and Young Beans from Rotting?
content: To prevent rotting, control the environment by providing shade during hot or rainy weather, ensuring proper ventilation, and protecting from storms. Maintain soil moisture with proper irrigation, avoid excess water, and use NPK fertilizer for nutrition. Apply Neem oil, insecticidal soap, or fungicide if needed, prune affected parts, and choose disease-resistant, high-quality varieties. For quick results, spray Neem oil or fungicide against flower thrips or Anthracnose and monitor regularly.

title: What Are the Biological Methods to Control Pod Borers?
content: Biological methods for pod borers in beans, peas, or similar plants include using natural enemies such as ladybird beetles that feed on larvae and adult borers. Neem oil disrupts the pest's hormones and feeding; spray 5% Neem oil or 10 ml Neem oil per liter of water 1-2 times a week. Homemade organic sprays like clove, garlic, onion paste, or turmeric + lemon can repel borers safely. Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) kills larval pod borers. Keeping tubs clean, using disease-free seeds, and planting resistant crops like coriander or mustard helps prevent infestations. Combining Neem oil with natural predators is the safest and most effective method.

title: How to Treat Paddy Husk Blight?
content: Use disease-tolerant varieties, plant seedlings at the right distance, apply balanced fertilizers, and avoid excess urea. If the disease occurs, burn the stubble of affected plants, remove infected plants, and spray fungicides such as propiconazole or tebuconazole.

title: What to Do if Cauliflower Leaves Turn Yellow Before Flowering?
content: Yellowing can be caused by excessive watering, nutrient deficiency (nitrogen, magnesium, iron), or viral disease. Apply balanced fertilizer, avoid overwatering, ensure well-drained soil, and prune diseased parts. Urea, MOP, and boron fertilizers can correct nutrient deficiencies.

title: Which Fertilizer Should Be Used When Lemon Leaves Turn Yellow from the Edges?
content: If older leaves are yellow, apply nitrogen-rich fertilizer. If young leaves are yellow, use sulfur-rich fertilizer. Potash fertilizer can be applied if initial symptoms of leaf burn disease appear.

title: What Should Be Done If Brown Spots Appear on Palm Leaves?
content: Spray 2-3 times with a mancozeb-type fungicide (e.g., Ridomil Gold) in 10 liters of water at 10-12 day intervals. Prune affected parts and keep the base of the plant clean and weed-free.

title: How to Remedy Root Rot in Kakrol Trees?
content: Prevent excess water accumulation, ensure soil aeration, and spray fungicides such as Emister Top or Folicur 25EC (1 ml per liter) or copper oxychloride (3 gm/liter). Neem oil can be applied, and reduce potassium or phosphorus fertilizers if necessary.

title: How to Prevent Squirrels from Damaging Fruit Trees Without Killing Them?
content: Repel squirrels by placing baubles on tree trunks, wrapping individual fruits in bags, or using sprays or naphthalene balls with odors squirrels dislike. Removing food sources such as bird feeders is also effective.

title: How to Reduce the Problem of Leeches in the Field?
content: Spray limbs or use salt- and tobacco-soaked water to reduce leeches. Wear knee-high boots or waterproof shoes, avoid excess morning watering, soak clothes and socks in tobacco water, and carry salt while walking. Keep the field clear of weeds, collect leeches and snails in wet sacks or rotten boards, and rake or burn the field after harvesting.

title: Why Are Sugarcane Plants Burning or Scorching?
content: Sugarcane plants burn or scorch due to diseases like leaf scorch, red rot, or red leaf spot, as well as climate or irrigation problems.

title: How to Treat Burning or Scorching in Sugarcane Plants?
content: Leaf scorch: spray carbendazim or mancozeb and remove affected plants. Red leaf spot: remove affected plants with roots and use disease-free seeds. Red rot: cut off affected leaves and stems, spray approved fungicide if needed. Avoid excess water, irrigate lightly, apply organic fertilizers, and collect seeds from disease-free land. Seek expert advice for widespread disease.

title: How to Control Guava Fly Larvae Inside Fruits?
content: Hang sex pheromone traps on fruit trees. Mix 20 ml of fenitrothion insecticide (e.g., Sumathion or Folithion) in 10 liters of water and spray 2-3 times every 10 days. Take care when applying insecticides.

title: Why Do Black and White Worms Appear on Rose Flower Buds?
content: Rose bud borer bores holes in flowers and buds. Cut off affected parts along with insects, keep the garden clean, and if infestation is severe, spray imidacloprid insecticide (e.g., Edmere 20 SL at 0.5 ml/liter of water).

title: Why Are Rose Leaves Turning Yellow and Developing Black Spots?
content: Black spots and yellowing are caused by the black spot fungus, which attacks leaves and stems. The fungus spreads via fallen leaves, especially when rain splashes spores onto new leaves. Yellow areas form around black spots, leading to leaf drop.

title: How to Remedy Black Spots and Yellowing on Rose Leaves?
content: Remove affected leaves and branches, use balanced fertilizers, and irrigate regularly. Cultivate disease-tolerant varieties. After collecting flowers, prune dead branches, infected fruit buds, and disease-affected parts. Spray the entire plant with fungicides and insecticides and inspect the garden regularly.

title: What Are Biological Methods to Control Rats Safely?
content: Use natural enemies like owls, foxes, badgers, wild cats, and snakes. Maintain awareness of their ecological importance. Additionally, remove rat shelters and food sources, use traps, and if necessary, apply chemicals carefully. An integrated approach combining biological and environmental measures is safest and most effective.

title: Why Is My Litchi Tree Not Flowering on the Roof?
content: Stop fertilizer and irrigation 2-3 months before bud formation. Avoid disturbing the tree, as new branches reduce bud formation. Litchi flowers on old branches grown in previous seasons (spring or summer) and blooms in Magh-Phalgun. Protect the tree from diseases and insects before flowering for proper bud development.

title: How to Make Chinese Oranges Sweet in a Roof Garden?
content: Select the right variety, provide adequate sunlight, grow in loamy soil, irrigate regularly (drip irrigation), use balanced fertilizers, especially magnesium sulfate and MOP after fruit set, and perform limb pruning or light pruning.

title: How to Control Insects Boring Flower Buds on Roses?
content: Tear off affected flower buds and keep the garden clean. If infestation is high, spray suitable pesticides like Pyrifos, Pyriban, or Malathion. Follow specific instructions carefully while applying pesticides.

title: How to Manage Curling Leaves on Garlic Caused by Thrips?
content: Identify thrips: females are gray-yellow, males dark brown, young ones yellow or white. Symptoms include silvery leaves, brown spots, and deformed tubers. Control using white sticky traps to increase spiders and apply approved pesticides at prescribed doses.

title: Why Are Most Cinnamon Tree Leaves Turning Black?
content: Black leaves are mainly caused by mealybugs or whiteflies. Prune and destroy affected leaves and tips. Spray 1 ml/l of Edmere mixed with water. Alternatively, use Tilt 250 EC (5 ml in 10 liters of water) and spray twice at 15-day intervals.

title: Why Are Reddish Rust-Like Raised Spots Appearing on Cinnamon Leaves?
content: Reddish rust-like spots indicate cinnamon red rust disease caused by green algae. Prune and destroy affected leaves and tips. Spray copper or Cupravit (20 g in 10 liters of water) twice at 15-day intervals.

title: Why Are White Powder-Like Objects Appearing on Bay Leaves?
content: White powder-like objects are caused by powdery mildew fungus. Keep the tree clean and prune regularly. Spray fungicides such as Tilt 250 EC (0.5 ml/l), Noin 50 WP (2 g/l), Xantho 5 EC (1 ml/l), or Wanzeb 80 WP (2 g/l) twice at 5-7 day intervals.

title: How to Treat Rotting Onion Bases?
content: Spray Tilt 250 EC or Rovral (0.5 ml per liter of water) twice at 10-12 day intervals to control base rot in onion plants.

title: Which Trap Is More Effective for Insect Control in Roof Gardens?
content: Yellow sticky traps are more effective than white traps in controlling insects in rooftop gardens.

title: Grape Leaves Are Turning Yellow with Holes - What Should I Do?
content: Yellow leaves with holes indicate flea beetle attack. Control with chlorpyrifos or lambda-cyhalothrin group insecticides as per recommended doses.

title: How to Reduce Soil Acidity in Rooftop Garden Tubs?
content: Increase soil pH by adding lime or limestone. Mix 10 grams into the tub soil, keeping it a little away from the plant base.

title: How to Remedy Mold or Rust on Tub Plants?
content: Red rust or mold: prune and destroy affected leaves and tips. Spray copper or Kupravit (20 g in 10 liters of water) twice at 15-day intervals.

title: Why Are Reddish Rust Spots on Orange Leaves, Stems, and Fruits?
content: Reddish rust spots indicate orange red rust disease caused by green algae. Prune and destroy affected leaves and tips, remove fallen leaves. Spray copper oxychloride (Kupravit) or Bordomix (100 g lime + 100 g mulberry in 10 l water) twice at 15-day intervals, especially at the beginning of the rainy season.

title: Why Is There White Cotton-Like Substance on Guava Leaves?
content: White cotton-like substance on guava leaves is caused by whiteflies, mealybugs, or scale insects. Remove affected leaves and destroy them. Use white glue boards or light traps. Spray 50 g of soap powder in 10 liters of water 2-3 times a week, optionally adding 5 bags of tobacco powder. Approved pesticides include Edmair (0.25-0.5 ml/l), Imitaf (0.25 ml/l), or Tuffgor/Ragab/Sanagar (2 ml/l).

title: Why Are There Worms Inside Ripe Guava Fruits?
content: Worms inside ripe guava are caused by fruit fly larvae. Prevent infestation by setting pheromone traps during flowering and bagging the fruits to stop insects from entering.

title: Why Are Betel Leaves Rotting?
content: Betel leaves rot due to Phytophthora parasitica, prevalent in low-magnesium, high-salinity soils and humid conditions. Avoid frequent irrigation. Spray Ridomil Gold or Companion (2 g/l) 2-3 times every 10 days, covering all plants and bases.

title: Why Are Betel Leaves Falling and Stems Drying?
content: Leaf fall and stem drying in betel is caused by the fungus Sclerotium rolfsii. Treat the vine before planting with Provex or Bavistin (2 g/l). If affected, spray the base with Provex or Bavistin (2 g/l).

title: Why Are Betel Leaves Turning Light in Color?
content: Light-colored betel leaves are caused by Fusarium oxysporum attacking the vascular tissue. Treat the vine before planting with Provex or Bavistin (2 g/l). Spray affected plant bases with Provex or Bavistin (2 g/l) to control infection.

title: How to Save Rich Tree Roots from Rotting?
content: For severe root rot in Rich trees, mix 20 g carbendazim (Emcozim) in 10 liters of water and spray 2-3 times every 5 days, with 12-15 day intervals between treatments.

title: Why Are Amra Tree Leaves Yellow and Drooping?
content: Check for hooted hopper insects sucking sap from young leaves and stems. If present, spray 2 ml of Rugor, Toughor, Sangor, Sumithion, Mipsin, or Sapsin per liter of water. If no insects, apply balanced fertilizers, irrigate regularly, prune affected parts, and spray cut parts with Bordeaux mixture or copper oxychloride (Kupravit 7 g/l). Spray Bavistin (1 g/l) three times at 7-10 day intervals when new leaves appear.

title: How to Treat Yellowed and Burnt Bay Leaves?
content: Yellow and burnt bay leaves indicate Gray Leaf Spot or Leaf Blight. Collect and burn affected leaves. Maintain soil moisture. Spray Propiconazole (Tilt 250 EC) or carbendazim (Autostin 2 g/l) 3-4 times in the afternoon at 10-12 day intervals.

title: Which Herbicide to Use for Weeds in Red Vegetable Fields?
content: Hand-picking weeds is the best method for red vegetable fields; avoid chemical herbicides where possible.

title: Why Are chilli Leaves Curling and Fruits Not Bearing?
content: Leaf curling and poor fruiting are caused by thrips and spider mites. Thrips make leaves boat-shaped; control with Dimethoate (Rugor, Tuffor 20 ml) or Imidachlorprid (Edmyr, Tido 10 ml), sprayed 2-3 times every 10 days. Mites are controlled using acaricides or sulfur fungicides like Thiovit, Cumulus, Vertimec, Omite, or Insaf (2 ml or 2 g/l).

title: Why Are Pomegranate Fruits Getting Smaller and How to Solve It?
content: Pomegranate fruits become smaller due to insufficient irrigation and lack of boron. Increase irrigation after fruit set and apply boron-containing fertilizer such as boric acid (40 g/tree). During fruit growth, spray soluble boron (2 g/l) on fruits and tree every 7-10 days.

title: How to Control White Insects Under Betel Leaves?
content: White insects under betel leaves are whiteflies (Aleurodes spp.) sucking sap. Spray neem oil or spider mite water, or malathion (2 ml/l). Alternatively, use tobacco leaf extract: soak 100 g tobacco stalks in 1 liter water overnight, mix 50 g soap, dilute with 8-9 liters of water, and spray. Stop leaf picking for one week.

title: Banana Leaves Rotting Due to Banchi-Top Disease: Cause and Remedy
content: Banchi-top disease in bananas is caused by a virus carried by jab beetles. Control the beetle with chlorpyrifos insecticides and uproot and destroy affected trees to prevent spread.

title: How Can a Roof Gardener Prevent Dengue?
content: Prevent dengue by avoiding water accumulation in tubs or garden. Plant a lemon tree on the balcony or roof every 8-10 tubs, as citric acid smell repels mosquitoes and prevents them from breeding.

title: Banana Tree Cracks and Insects: What to Do?
content: Uproot and burn affected banana trees. Do not use their saplings as seedlings. Improve drainage to prevent water accumulation and reduce disease and insect growth.

title: Why Are Papaya Leaf Juice and Pomegranate Beneficial for Dengue Patients?
content: Papaya leaf juice contains chymopapin and papain, which help normalize blood platelet levels and improve circulation. Pomegranate also supports recovery, increasing the ability to fight dengue.

title: Lemon Tree Tips Dying with Curled Leaves: Solution
content: Cut dead and some healthy parts neatly with a sharp knife. Apply Bordeaux paste (100 g lime + 100 g mulberry in 1 liter water). Spray copper oxychloride fungicide (4 g/l) 1-2 times every 7-10 days and keep the garden clean to control tip dieback.

title: Root Rot in Pepper Tree: How to Treat
content: Root rot in pepper trees is fungal. Mix 20 g carbendazim (Emcozim) in 10 liters of water and spray thoroughly 2-3 times every 12-15 days, taking precautions while spraying.

title: chilli Plant Wilting: Causes and Solutions
content: chilli wilts due to damping-off or Fusarium wilt. For damping-off, create high, well-drained seedbeds, treat seeds with formaldehyde or Trichoderma, and apply Provex-200 or Ridomil Gold. For Fusarium wilt, cultivate on high land, treat seeds with Provex-200 or Bevistin, apply lime and potash, and if needed, formalin. Spray affected plants with Bevistin or Cupravit (2 g/l).

title: How to Treat Diseases, Pests, or Insects in Sweet Pumpkin Plants
content: For curling leaves or insect attack, spray neem leaf juice, red chilli powder, and soapy water. For powdery mildew, spray a milk-water mixture (1:10). Remove affected leaves regularly.

title: Does Almond Meal Help Prevent Root Rot?
content: Using almond meal in the required amount reduces harmful bacteria in the soil, lowering the risk of root rot in plants.

title: How to Prevent Mealybug Attack on Guava Trees?
content: Mealybugs weaken guava trees by sucking sap from young leaves, tips, and fruits. Early control includes spraying with strong water, removing affected parts, and controlling ants. Spray soapy water or neem seed water 2-3 times every 10 days. In heavy infestations, spray 7-10 ml of imidachlorprid per 10 liters of water. Cleanliness and balanced fertilization help prevent attacks.

title: Small Holes in Rice Pumpkin: How to Solve It?
content: Small holes in rice pumpkin are caused by pumpkin fly larvae eating the pulp. Collect and destroy affected fruits, cover young fruits with paper or polythene, set 3 pheromone traps per 10% of plants, use poison bait if necessary, and spray cypermethrin (1 ml/l) for heavy infestations. Avoid consuming sprayed fruits for 15 days. Proper land cultivation destroys pupae.

title: What to Do If Fungal Disease Increases During Rainy Season?
content: Spray Dithane M-45 (2 g/l), Mancozeb (2 g/l), or Copper Oxychloride (0.2%) every 10-12 days. For insect control, use neem oil, soapy water spray, sticky traps, or environmental control. For fungal protection, apply Trichoderma or organic fungicides.

title: Why Is a White Fungus Layer Appearing in the Tub?
content: White fungus in tubs is caused by excess moisture, poor drainage, and decomposed old organic fertilizer. Remove the top soil, use fresh soil, dry the tub in the sun, and spray fungicide as needed.

title: Which Insects Cause the Most Damage During Monsoon?
content: During the monsoon, fruit flies, whiteflies, mealybugs, thrips, and aphids cause the most damage due to high humidity.

title: Effective Methods to Control Fruit Flies
content: Collect and bury fallen fruits, use traps or poison baits, sprinkle bleaching powder under trees, spray neem oil if necessary. For heavy infestations, use Sumathion (2 ml/l).

title: Why Do Leaves Turn Yellow During Monsoon and How to Fix?
content: Leaves turn yellow in monsoon due to excess water, nitrogen deficiency, poor drainage, or fungal diseases. Reduce water, add soil at the base, spray fungicide, and apply small amounts of urea or compost.

title: What to Do If the Base of a Plant Becomes Soft in Rainy Season?
content: Change the top 2-3 inches of soil, ensure the drain hole is clear, dry the pot in the sun, and stabilize the plant with supports or poles, as soft soil can cause the plant to tilt.

title: Solution to Bay Leaf Leaf Scorch Disease
content: Leaf scorch causes small yellow-brown spots on bay leaves that merge and burn leaves. Spray tebuconazole + trifloxystrobin (Nativo 5 g) or propiconazole (Tilt 5 ml/10 l) 2-3 times every 10-12 days. Take care while spraying.

title: Why Is There No Water Inside the Coconut?
content: Lack of water inside a coconut is due to sterile or dumb coconuts caused by incomplete pollination, pregnancy problems, or nutritional deficiencies, especially potassium and boron.

title: How to Solve the Problem of No Water Inside Coconut?
content: Apply 2 cloves of rotted cow dung or organic fertilizer, 300 g urea, 250 g TSP, 300 g MOP, and 50 g boron fertilizer in a circle at a distance of one hand from the base of the coconut tree.

title: Why Are Papaya Fruits Large and Round?
content: Papaya fruits may become large and round due to boron deficiency, pollination errors, or difficulties in fruit setting, which lead to deformed fruit shapes.

title: How to Fix Deformation in Papaya Fruits?
content: Spray 0.5 ml of Liberal boron or 2.5 g boric acid powder in 0.5 liters of water twice every 7 days. Additionally, mix 1 drop of the biostimulant Litosen per liter of water and spray 2-3 times every 21 days.

title: What Is the Leaf and Stem Borer in Bananas?
content: Leaf and stem borers make small holes in banana leaves, cause yellowing and slow drying, and dig cylindrical paths inside the stem, slowing tree growth and reducing yield.

title: Banana Tree Leaves Turning Yellow and Dying Remedy
content: Yellowing and dying banana trees indicate Panama disease. The affected trees should be uprooted and burned to prevent disease spread.

title: Why Are Dragon Fruit Flowers Falling?
content: Dragon fruit flowers fall due to immature pollen, poor nutrition, excessive rain, or over-irrigation. Collect pollen from flowers blooming at the same time and apply it to female flowers for artificial pollination to ensure fruit set.

title: What to Do About French Bean Root Rot?
content: Uproot and destroy affected plants, maintain good drainage, and if infestation is heavy, spray Rovral at 2 g/l on plants and soil.

title: Why Are Ants Found Near Aphids?
content: Aphids secrete honeydew, attracting ants. Leaves may turn black due to honeydew accumulation, explaining the presence of ants near aphid attacks.

title: How to Treat Black Spots on Mango Leaves?
content: Cut and burn affected or dead parts, collect fallen leaves and fruits, spray 2 g/l Mencozeb on buds or young fruits. Spray 3-4 times every 15 days starting 15 days before harvest. After harvest, soak mangoes in hot water (55°C, 5 min) and keep dry. Maintain cleanliness and regular spraying during heavy rains.

title: Which Method Is Most Effective for Controlling Flies in Pumpkin Crops?
content: Pheromone traps are very effective for controlling pumpkin flies. Use one trap every 4-5 plants. Place the trap 1 foot above the canopy on a wooden pole, change the water regularly, and clean dead insects. The pheromone lure lasts for 2 months and can be used across all pumpkin crops.

title: How to Control Mango Flies?
content: Control mango flies by bagging fruits, promptly removing damaged fruits, preparing poison bait (100 g mango juice + 5 g Vitabril + 100 ml water), installing Bactro-D type pheromone traps, and spraying Fenitrothion group insecticides such as Sumithion (2.4 ml/l) or Toughgar (2 ml/l) in the late afternoon if needed.

title: How to Reduce Primary Stage Fruit Drop in Lychee?
content: To reduce primary stage fruit drop in lychee, ensure balanced pollination, proper nutrition (especially boron), controlled irrigation, protection from adverse weather, and suppression of pests and diseases. Increase pollinator attendance, apply light boron or micronutrient sprays, avoid overwatering, and remove infected fruits quickly.

title: What Is the Shoe Coat Disease of Bari Mango 4?
content: Shoe Coat Disease is caused by fungal attack. Leaves, stems, and buds develop gray-brown stains, flowers fall, and fruits rot. Remedies: cut and burn affected branches at the end of the mango season, apply Bordeaux mixture to cut parts, and spray Dithane M-45 or Tilt 250 EC before flower formation to prevent recurrence.

title: How to Suppress Coconut Mites?
content: Control coconut mites by destroying infected young fruits, keeping tree tops clean, spraying Omite/Sumite/Vertimet acaricides at 1.5-2 ml/l in four stages (Ashwin-Kartik to Jyishta-Ashadh), and using Bavistin or Mencozeb at 2 g/l in the first two sprays to reduce mite infestation and fruit drop.

title: Why Do Lemon Fruits Fall at the Primary Stage?
content: Lemon fruits often drop early due to excess water, nutritional deficiencies, lack of sunlight, or sudden weather changes, causing small fruits to fall prematurely.

title: How to Prevent Lemon Fruit Drop?
content: Prevent lemon fruit drop by avoiding overwatering, providing at least 6 hours of direct sunlight daily, applying organic fertilizers regularly, controlling insect infestation, irrigating lightly to prevent water accumulation, and using grow lights if grown indoors.

title: Why Are Okra Leaves Eaten and Look Like a Grid?
content: To control leaf-eating insects on okra, collect and destroy affected plants and leaves, maintain field cleanliness, set 1-2 light traps, and spray insecticides such as Novolution 10% EC (1 ml/l), Carbaryl 50% WP (2.5 g/l), or Malathion 50% EC (2 ml/l) if needed.

title: How to Control Leaf-Eating Insects on Mango Trees?
content: Control mango leaf-eating insects by collecting and destroying affected leaves and plants, keeping the garden clean, setting 1-2 light traps to capture adults, and spraying Novolution 10% EC (1 ml/l), Carbaryl 50% WP (2.5 g/l), or Malathion 50% EC (2 ml/l) if necessary.

title: Why Are Insects Found Inside Mango Fruits Even Without External Wounds?
content: Insects inside mango fruits without visible external wounds are caused by mango flies laying eggs inside the fruit, which hatch into larvae that feed internally.

title: Why Do Pepper Tree Leaves Curl?
content: Pepper tree leaves curl due to insect attacks or stress. To control, remove waste fruits, bag the fruits or cover them with polythene, remove affected fruits, install Bactro-D pheromone traps, and spray Fenitrothion group insecticides such as Sumathion (2.4 ml/l) or Toughgar (2 ml/l) in the afternoon.

title: How to Control Leaf Curl Disease in chilli Plants?
content: To control leaf curl disease in chilli plants, collect seeds from healthy plants, avoid using diseased seedlings, cover seedlings with mosquito nets, destroy affected plants and surrounding host plants, and spray Malathion insecticide during the seedling stage.

title: How to Prevent Mango Fruit Shedding?
content: To prevent mango fruit shedding, apply regular irrigation, spray magnol after bud break, use boron fertilizer, apply balanced fertilizer before and after monsoon, apply 50 g dolochun per plant annually, add adequate organic fertilizer, and spray fungicides and insecticides once a year.

title: Impact of Using Pheromone Traps Instead of Pesticides in Vegetable Farming
content: Pheromone traps help in safe vegetable production by reducing the harmful effects of pesticides. They prevent environmental damage, reduce health risks, and save money by lowering pesticide usage, while effectively controlling pests.

title: How to Prevent Mealybugs in a Roof Garden?
content: To prevent mealybugs, handpick and destroy them in the morning or evening, spray neem or clove water, and put salt or lime around the plants. Plant companion plants like coriander, mint, or radish, remove dead leaves, and ensure adequate sunlight and air circulation to reduce mealybug attacks.

title: How to Control Giant Mealybug on Mango Trees?
content: Wrap the base of the mango trunk with polythene in April to trap adult females, collect and burn them. Remove and sun-dry soil in May-June to destroy eggs. Apply adhesive or grease bands on the trunk to prevent nymphs from climbing. Spray approved insecticides like Ripcord 10 EC (1 ml/l), Marsal 25 EC (3 ml/l), or Confidor 70 WG (0.4 g/l) three times at 7-day intervals. Create small canals with kerosene-mixed water to prevent adult spread.

title: Why Do Litchi Buds Fall During Storms?
content: Bud drop in litchi can occur due to dry weather or hormonal deficiency. To prevent it, spray Planofix or Miraculan at recommended doses when fruits are pea to marble-sized, followed by zinc sulfate (10 g/l) after bud formation. Ensure regular care and timely pest and disease control.

title: How to Increase Fruit Set in Orange Trees?
content: Fruit set in orange trees can be increased by providing optimal temperature and soil moisture, preventing excess growth due to improper pruning or fertilization, controlling tree spacing, and protecting trees from heavy rain and strong winds. Managing nitrogen levels and proper pruning also improve fruit set and yield.

title: Effective Ways to Control Watermelon Leaf Miner
content: Collect and destroy affected leaves to prevent larvae spread. Use yellow sticky traps to catch adult insects. For heavy infestations, spray cypermethrin at 1 ml/liter thoroughly on affected plants. Monitor regularly and re-spray as necessary to control leaf miner effectively.

title: Impact of Using Pheromone Traps Instead of Pesticides in Vegetable Farming
content: Pheromone traps help in safe vegetable production by reducing the harmful effects of pesticides. They prevent environmental damage, reduce health risks, and save money by lowering pesticide usage, while effectively controlling pests.

title: How to Prevent Mealybugs in a Roof Garden?
content: To prevent mealybugs, handpick and destroy them in the morning or evening, spray neem or clove water, and put salt or lime around the plants. Plant companion plants like coriander, mint, or radish, remove dead leaves, and ensure adequate sunlight and air circulation to reduce mealybug attacks.

title: How to Control Giant Mealybug on Mango Trees?
content: Wrap the base of the mango trunk with polythene in April to trap adult females, collect and burn them. Remove and sun-dry soil in May-June to destroy eggs. Apply adhesive or grease bands on the trunk to prevent nymphs from climbing. Spray approved insecticides like Ripcord 10 EC (1 ml/l), Marsal 25 EC (3 ml/l), or Confidor 70 WG (0.4 g/l) three times at 7-day intervals. Create small canals with kerosene-mixed water to prevent adult spread.

title: Why Do Litchi Buds Fall During Storms?
content: Bud drop in litchi can occur due to dry weather or hormonal deficiency. To prevent it, spray Planofix or Miraculan at recommended doses when fruits are pea to marble-sized, followed by zinc sulfate (10 g/l) after bud formation. Ensure regular care and timely pest and disease control.

title: How to Increase Fruit Set in Orange Trees?
content: Fruit set in orange trees can be increased by providing optimal temperature and soil moisture, preventing excess growth due to improper pruning or fertilization, controlling tree spacing, and protecting trees from heavy rain and strong winds. Managing nitrogen levels and proper pruning also improve fruit set and yield.

title: Effective Ways to Control Watermelon Leaf Miner
content: Collect and destroy affected leaves to prevent larvae spread. Use yellow sticky traps to catch adult insects. For heavy infestations, spray cypermethrin at 1 ml/liter thoroughly on affected plants. Monitor regularly and re-spray as necessary to control leaf miner effectively.

title: Jackfruit Tree Is Not Bearing Fruit - What Should Be Done?
content: If a jackfruit tree does not bear fruit, the main reasons are poor pollination and micronutrient deficiency, especially boron. To solve this problem, ensure proper pollination and spray boron fertilizer at the rate of 2 grams per liter of water. Fertilizer application should be adjusted according to the age of the tree and applied near the canopy area.

title: Is There Any Pheromone Trap Available for Use in Litchi Gardens?
content: At present, there is no pheromone trap specifically developed for litchi pests. Pheromone traps are mainly used to control fruit flies in other fruit crops.

title: What Steps Can Be Taken to Control Coconut Weevil?
content: Coconut weevil damages both seedlings and mature trees by eating roots, climbing the trunk and destroying bark and crown tissues, which can kill the tree. In weevil-prone areas, applying Sevin powder or Regenta at the base of the plant during fertilizer application twice a year is effective in controlling this pest.

title: Eggplant Seedling Stem Is Bursting After Transplanting - What Should Be Done?
content: Stem bursting and leaf death of eggplant seedlings a few days after transplanting is usually caused by fungal infection. If the disease is severe, spray carbendazim-based fungicides (such as Noin or Emcozim 20 g) or propiconazole-based fungicides (such as Tilt 5 ml) mixed in 10 liters of water, 2-3 times at 10-12 day intervals. Caution should be taken while spraying.

title: What Is the Control Method for Blossom End Rot of Gourd?
content: Blossom end rot of gourd is mainly caused by calcium deficiency and acidic soil conditions. Rotting starts from the bottom of young fruits without worm infestation. To control the disease, provide moderate irrigation, apply 50-80 g gypsum per pit, and use 4 kg dolochun per hundred in acidic soil. Balanced fertilization, crop rotation and quick removal of affected fruits are essential preventive measures.

title: What Are the Benefits of Using Trichoderma Fungus?
content: Trichoderma is a beneficial soil fungus that suppresses harmful fungi, bacteria and nematodes. It improves soil structure, increases water retention, reduces irrigation costs and enhances soil fertility. Using tricho-organic fertilizers can reduce chemical fertilizer and pesticide use by 40-60%. It is effective for seed treatment, soil-borne disease control and increasing crop yield in toxin-free farming.

title: What Should Be Done in Toxin-Free Vegetable Farming?
content: For toxin-free vegetable farming, seeds should be treated before sowing using garlic or horseradish extract. Clean cultivation must be maintained. Sex pheromone traps should be used for cucurbit crops and brinjal. Sticky or yellow traps help control other pests. Ash application on bean plants, soapy water spray for jassids, and removing excess flowers improve plant health and reduce pest attacks naturally.

title: How Long Should Seeds Be Soaked in Vitavax or Provax for Treatment?
content: When using Vitavax or Provax for seed treatment, seeds should be soaked in water for 30 minutes to 1 hour. Small seeds require shorter soaking time, while large or hard seeds can be soaked for up to one hour. After soaking, seeds should be strained, dried and then sown.

title: What Is the Reason for Litchi Leaves Curling?
content: Litchi leaves curl mainly due to water stress, excessive sunlight, attack by leaf miner or leaf roller insects, and nitrogen or micronutrient deficiency.

title: What Should Be Done If Litchi Leaves Curl Up?
content: If litchi leaves curl up, ensure regular irrigation and apply light doses of urea or NPK fertilizer as needed. If insect infestation is present, spray Proclaim or Decis at 7-10 day intervals to control leaf miner or leaf roller insects.

title: Why Do Lower Leaves of a Litchi Tree Turn Yellow and Die?
content: Lower leaves of a litchi tree usually die due to nutrient deficiency, fungal diseases like gummosis or anthracnose, or weak root conditions.

title: How to Treat Drying Lower Leaves of a Litchi Tree?
content: Apply good compost at the base, avoid waterlogging, and spray copper oxychloride or mancozeb if fungal infection is suspected.

title: How Harmful Are Aphids at the Base of a Litchi Tree?
content: Aphids at the base damage roots and the trunk, disrupt water and nutrient transport, weaken the tree, and may kill new leaves and shoots.

title: How to Control Aphids at the Base of a Litchi Tree?
content: Pour kerosene or gasoline into aphid holes if needed, apply chlorpyrifos to soil, and keep the base area clean and dry.

title: How to Identify Leaf Curl Due to Insects or Nutrient Deficiency?
content: In insect attack, curled leaves show crooked spots and larvae inside. In nutrient deficiency, leaves become pale, small, and the whole plant weakens.

title: Can Root Weevils Kill a Litchi Tree?
content: Yes, prolonged weevil infestation can destroy roots, block nutrient uptake, and eventually kill the litchi tree if untreated.

title: Best Treatment for Fungal Diseases in Litchi Trees
content: Prune infected parts, spray copper oxychloride, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin every 15 days, and keep the tree base clean.

title: What Fertilizer Keeps a Litchi Tree Healthy?
content: Apply 10-15 kg compost annually, use age-based NPK fertilizers, and add small amounts of boron and zinc during winter and spring.

title: How to Treat Litchi Trees Affected by Both Fungi and Insects?
content: Spray insecticide on the first day and fungicide the next day. Do not mix chemicals to avoid incompatibility issues.

title: What Are Effective Home Remedies for Aphids?
content: Soapy water, lime-salt solution, kerosene application, or hot water on dry soil can reduce aphids, though approved pesticides work better for large plants.

title: How to Control Viral Diseases in Cucumber Plants?
content: Spray neem insecticide at 2-3 ml per liter or imidacloprid at 0.25 ml per liter to control virus-spreading insects.

title: Which Insect Cuts Young Mango Leaves?
content: The mango leaf-cutting weevil is responsible; it is gray-brown, long-bodied, and damages tender leaves.

title: How Does the Mango Leaf-Cutting Weevil Damage Trees?
content: The female lays eggs under leaves and cuts near leaf tips, causing young leaves to fall and stunting plant growth.

title: When Is Mango Most Vulnerable to Weevil Attack?
content: Weevils attack mango trees most during the seedling and active growth stages.

title: How to Identify Weevil Damage on Mango Trees?
content: Rounded or crescent-shaped cuts on young leaves and presence of long brown insects indicate weevil infestation.

title: Do Weevils Prefer Young Mango Leaves?
content: Yes, weevils feed exclusively on new and tender mango leaves.

title: Effective Chemical Control for Mango Leaf-Cutting Weevils
content: Spray Fenitrathion, Carbaryl, or Cartap at recommended doses every 10 days when new leaves emerge, preferably in calm weather.

title: Are There Organic or Home Remedies to Control Mango Weevil?
content: Organic control methods for mango weevil include using blue light traps, shaking trees in the evening and collecting insects on polythene sheets, and spraying neem oil or mild soapy water when infestation is low.

title: Why Is Leaf Miner Infestation Increasing in Malta Seedlings?
content: Leaf miner infestation increases due to tender new leaves. Early control includes removing and burning infested leaves and using yellow sticky traps coated with burnt mobil oil.

title: How to Control Leaf Miner in Malta Plants?
content: For severe infestation, spray dimethoate (Tufgor) or Sabikron at 3 ml per liter of water in the late afternoon. Spray twice over 7 days and weekly during new leaf growth, avoiding spraying during fruiting.

title: What Are Organic Pesticides and Why Are They Important?
content: Organic pesticides are derived from plants or natural sources. They are important because excessive chemical pesticide use causes soil, water, and air pollution, while organic options help maintain environmental balance.
